name: FormCompiler
title: the one place every FormAI app is built, signed and released
summary: Push a compile branch, get a draft release: FormCompiler builds, signs and releases every FormAI app and writes the catalogue FormPortal reads.
lede: FormCompiler builds and releases the FormAI apps. The app repositories build nothing: when an app is ready, its owner pushes a branch named compile_vX.Y.Z, and FormCompiler checks it, builds the app on every platform the app lists, signs it and opens a draft release. Publishing the draft hands the release to a private pipeline that refreshes the update feed and the family catalogue FormPortal reads.
runs_on: GitHub Actions, with Python 3.11 or later for its scripts
checks: Watches every registered app for compile_vX.Y.Z branches every hour, or at once from the Run workflow button.
Refuses a branch whose version file disagrees or whose own checks did not conclude success on that commit.
Builds each app on the platforms its registry file lists, plus phone apps, tarballs, Flatpak, server binaries or a container image where listed.
Opens a draft release on the app's own repository with SHA256SUMS.txt; the update feeds and signed catalogue are published by a private companion pipeline.

facts.dd: GitHub Actions and Python 3 standard library scripts; cryptography only to sign the catalogue
vX.Y.Z drafts on each app's own repository; a published release is never overwritten

chapters.title: Push a branch, get a draft
chapters.text: From an app's repository, after the version bump is on main, push compile_vX.Y.Z from main's head. The next watch run checks the branch, starts the build and leaves a draft release to review and publish. A second push to the same branch rebuilds and refreshes the draft.

chapters.title: One file describes each app
chapters.text: apps/<app>.json says how to read the app's version, which checks must pass, its platforms, toolchain and build commands, extra jobs, release assets, update files and its catalogue entry. scripts/registry.py check validates every file against the contract in docs/REGISTRY.md.

chapters.title: Signing in one place
chapters.text: The Apple Developer ID and notarization, the Windows code-signing certificate and the updater key are FormCompiler secrets only; no app repository holds one. Until they are set, macOS builds are signed ad hoc and Windows builds are unsigned.

features.title: The watch
features.text: watch.yml runs every hour (minute 17 UTC) and from the Run workflow button, over every app in apps/*.json.
bullets: Finds compile_v* branches in every registered app
Skips what is already published, drafted or running
Refuses a wrong version or a failed check
Waits while the app's checks are still running
Starts release.yml for the app, commit and version

features.title: Checked before anything builds
features.text: The branch name, the version file at that commit and the app's own check workflows are checked, and the same rules run again at the start of each release.
bullets: The app's checks must have concluded success on that commit
Pre-releases work the same way, as in compile_v1.97.0-rc.1
A published version is refused; bump the version to release again

features.title: Every platform the app lists
features.text: desktop-release.yml builds each platform the registry names, with the app's own build contract or its own commands and a post-build hook.
bullets: macOS on Apple silicon, Intel and universal
Windows on x64, ARM64 and x86
Linux on x64 and ARM64
Experimental platforms and per-platform environment

features.title: Extra jobs
features.text: Beyond the desktop matrix, an app's registry file can ask for more, built in the same release run.
bullets: Phone apps
A riscv64 tarball and a Flatpak
Server binaries
A container image

features.title: Drafts, never surprises
features.text: Every release starts as a draft tagged vX.Y.Z on the app's own repository, titled <title> <version>, with SHA256SUMS.txt and release notes taken from the app's CHANGELOG.
bullets: A rebuilt draft is refreshed in place
A published release is never overwritten
A person publishes; nothing ships on its own

features.title: Update feeds
features.text: The private publishing pipeline writes the app's <app>-updates feed from the published release, using this repository's scripts.
bullets: Signed updater bundles when the updater key is set
The updater public key is written into each app's build
Which app a tag belongs to is read from the tag

features.title: One catalogue for the family
features.text: Public files are served from https://dl.formai.studio, with the catalogue at catalog/apps.json and catalog/apps.json.sig.
bullets: Ed25519 signature over the catalogue
Its public half goes into FormPortal's core/catalog_keys.txt
scripts/catalog.py builds the catalogue and makes a key pair

features.title: No secrets in the apps
features.text: FormCompiler watches the app repositories itself, so no app holds a token for it. Every secret and variable lives in FormCompiler's repository, and all are optional.
bullets: A read-only token for the app repositories while they are private
Apple signing and notarization, the Windows certificate
The Tauri updater key and the token that tells the publishing pipeline about a release

features.title: Pinned actions and a self-check
features.text: Every third-party action is pinned to a full commit SHA, and self-check.yml runs actionlint (checksum-verified), the registry check, the scripts and the text rules.
bullets: actionlint verified by checksum
scripts/registry.py check over every registry file
No expressions inside run scripts; values reach the shell through env

features.title: Scripts you can run by hand
features.text: The nineteen scripts use only Python's standard library, apart from signing the catalogue, and each can be run from a terminal.
bullets: registry.py check validates every registry file
watch.py --dry-run shows what the watch would start
plan.py works out version, tag and platform matrix from an app's root
catalog.py build writes the catalogue from the published releases

requirements: Python 3.11 or later for the scripts
docs.install:
Write apps/<app>.json from docs/REGISTRY.md and add 'compile_v*' to the push branches of the app's check workflow, then:
python3 scripts/registry.py check
python3 scripts/registry.py config --app <app>

topics.title: The registry contract
topics.text: docs/REGISTRY.md documents every field of apps/<app>.json: top level, toolchain, build, extras, image, updater and catalog.

topics.title: Releasing an app
topics.text: Push compile_vX.Y.Z from main's head after the version bump, review the draft on the app's own Releases page, then publish it.

topics.title: Secrets and variables
topics.text: The README lists every optional secret and variable: the app token, Apple signing and notarization, the Windows certificate, the updater key and the pipeline dispatch token.

topics.title: The scheduled watch
topics.text: If GitHub disables the scheduled watch after 60 days without activity, re-enable it under Actions, watch; every published release commits releases.json, which counts as activity.

items: Every app release is drafted on the app's own repository, tagged vX.Y.Z, and FormCompiler keeps no app release
Release files are assembled by a job with no credential, and a separate publish job writes them
The publish job attests the provenance of SHA256SUMS.txt and form-app.json
Publishing to the download store, the update feeds, the catalogue signature and yanks move to a private companion pipeline
feed.yml, yank.yml and docs/GO_PUBLIC.md are removed; the scripts stay
release.yml tells the pipeline about each release it publishes with a repository dispatch
A file_names setting in a registry entry keeps an app's own names
FormRanker is FormBench: the repository and the registry entry are renamed
